text: 🇲🇽⚖️ The headlines called it a setback. Sheinbaum called it continuity. "If the US decides today not to extend 16 years, the treaty holds for the next 10 — its term to 2036 — and it's reviewed every year." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 Washington's refusal to extend USMCA to 2042 was read abroad as a loss. Mexico read it as the deal simply continuing on its own terms. It goes into the July 20 review with three aims: cut external dependency, fix review timelines, clarify the process. Negotiating from calm, not urgency.

🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico is going to have a very important opportunity in these years." "The US is changing its trade relationship with every country… I think Mexico will have a very important opportunity these years." — Marcelo Ebrard, Economy Secretary — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 As Washington reshuffles its trade ties, South Korea, Japan and Canada have signaled interest in deeper commercial links with Mexico. Diversification isn't a threat — it's leverage.

🇲🇽⚽ The UK warned its fans away from seven Mexican states. Sheinbaum: "It's safe to visit the country." "It is safe to visit the country; they have no problem." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 Britain issued a travel alert ahead of the Mexico–England match on July 5. Sheinbaum pushed back plainly. On Mexico City's Reforma, where four people died in Tuesday's celebrations, the city is adding screens to spread out crowds. World Cup 2026 plays on.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 71.2 tons of aid to earthquake-hit Venezuela — and Mexican rescuers still on the ground. "Essentially everything we send goes through National Defense." — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 After quakes that killed over 2,000 people, Mexico has delivered 71.2 tons of food, medicine and power plants. Its 'Yumare' rescue team pulled 2 survivors and recovered 40 bodies between June 26 and July 1 — and rescued a dog. Another Navy ship departs Friday. Solidarity, no conditions.

🔥🇲🇽 Washington says a cartel funded Mexican campaigns. Sheinbaum: show the evidence. "The part about campaigns — we were never informed of that. What evidence do they have?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 The US Treasury claimed fuel-theft money tied to the CJNG financed political campaigns — without notifying Mexico first. Sheinbaum noted that when Mexico seeks extraditions, the US demands proof: evidence should be requested on both sides. Mexico's financial unit has already frozen the accounts named.

🇲🇽🏭 "If we want to cut the deficit, we have to produce more in North America." "How do we produce on this side — the US, Mexico, Canada? If we don't solve that, we'll never solve the deficit." — Marcelo Ebrard, Economy Secretary — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 Ebrard reframed the trade fight around production, not tariffs: the components Mexico still imports — up to 90% in some lines — are the real target. It's the logic of Plan México: build the supply chain at home instead of importing it.

🇲🇽⚖️ The US won't extend USMCA to 2042. Mexico's answer: fine — it runs to 2036, and we review it every year. "The Treaty stays in force until 2036. We'll do annual reviews." — Marcelo Ebrard, Economy Secretary — Mañanera, July 2, 2026 At the first-ever trilateral meeting of Mexico, Canada and the US, Washington declined a 16-year extension. Mexico negotiates from strength: over 80% of its exports enter the US duty-free, with some of the lowest effective tariffs of any US partner. Next bilateral round: July 20, Mexico City.

🇲🇽💵 <u>ANALYSTS CUT MEXICO'S 2026 INFLATION FORECAST TO 4.20%</u>

Banxico's survey of 41 private-sector analysts just lowered the year-end inflation forecast to 4.20%, down from 4.35%. The trigger: first-half June consumer prices fell at a pace unseen in over two decades, dragging annual inflation to 3.55% — the lowest since October. Growth held at 1.1%, benchmark rate seen closing the year at 6.50%.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S 13-PROJECT PUSH FOR TECH SOVEREIGNTY: NATIONAL EV + STATE SUPERCOMPUTER</u>

SECIHTI presented 13 projects to Congress to "consolidate technological independence and knowledge ownership in Mexico." Two flagships: Olinia, a 100% Mexican-engineered electric car headed for mass production in 2027, and Coatlicue, the country's first state-owned supercomputer, built with 10 public universities and research centers.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX REABSORBS 40 SUBSIDIARIES — 2013 REFORM BEING REVERSED</u>

Sheinbaum is folding Pemex's ~40 scattered subsidiaries back into one vertically integrated state company, capping output at 1.8 million barrels a day and targeting financial autonomy by 2027. "Pemex will return to efficient operation, without so many scattered boards." The new petroleum laws "substantially reverse" Peña Nieto's 2013 reform that opened the oil to multinationals competing against the nation's own company.
